headlines.title: Nearly half of U.S. teens ages 13 to 17 say they’ve gambled in the last year, survey finds
headlines.description: The report’s lead author said minors now have more access to gambling through “video games, sports broadcasts and other products.”

headlines.title: Many with ACA coverage face a new crisis in 2027: Insurers fleeing the market
headlines.description: Courtney Mroch was already paying a high price for health insurance when she learned her insurer, Cigna, was pulling out of Tennessee’s Affordable Care Act marketplace.

headlines.title: MAHA fractures deepen as some RFK Jr. followers turn into harsh critics
headlines.description: A scorecard from MAHA activists suggests the Trump administration has broken most of its promises to the movement. The “burn feels especially raw,” one prominent activist said.

headlines.title: FDA plans to update nutritional rules for infant formula
headlines.description: The Food and Drug Administration plans to introduce new rules around what nutrients must be added to infant formula. The changes the FDA plans to propose, which were shared in advance with NBC News, would tweak the minimum and maximum levels of four nutrients: iodine, manganese, vitamin A and vitamin D.

headlines.title: Pat Croce Shares Lessons From ‘Enjoy Yourself Now!’
headlines.description: Pat Croce, the enthusiastic former president and co-owner of the Philadelphia 76ers who once climbed the Walt Whitman Bridge to hang the team’s banner, joins TODAY talk about his new book “Enjoy Yourself Now! 66 Sacred Shifts to Instantly Awaken the Peaceful Presence Within You.”

headlines.title: Clocks Change This Weekend: What You Can Do Now to Adjust
headlines.description: This weekend, Daylight Saving Time ends and even though we “fall back” and gain an extra hour, it can still mess with our body clocks. Dr. Mike Varshavski, board certified family medicine physician, joins TODAY to share ways to keep your sleep cycle on track.

headlines.title: Health Concerns Raised for Elementary School Near Data Centers
headlines.description: An elementary school in Loudoun County, Virginia is nearly surrounded by 11 data centers and community members are concerned about the pollution that be might produced and what their kids might be breathing. NBC’s Stephanie Gosk reports for TODAY.

headlines.title: Everything you need for an at-home Korean scalp facial
headlines.description: The Korean scalp facial can be used to treat scalp issues like oiliness, dryness, thinning hair and more — I asked experts for the best way to try one at home.

headlines.title: 81+ actually good gifts for women that go beyond jewelry and silk robes
headlines.description: Shop the best gifts for women in 2026, including picks from Apple, Ugg and more for every budget, all curated by NBC Selected shopping experts.

headlines.title: Can red light really help you sleep? Here’s what experts say
headlines.description: Red light is touted for everything from skin to sleep. Sleep experts explain whether it really helps you rest, how to use it and what to buy if you want to try it.

headlines.title: Running in the dark? This reflective running gear will help you stay safe
headlines.description: Running before sunrise or after sunset requires extra safety precautions. Here’s the best reflective running gear and LED lights to protect yourself, plus expert tips.

headlines.title: Patrick Stewart Died After Battling Alzheimer’s and Lewy Body Dementia. What to Know
headlines.description: Legendary actor Patrick Stewart passed away this week after a brief experience with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia. What to know about the conditions.
